Exercise 15.7.17 — Evaluate the Triple Integral

Problem. Evaluate the triple integral ∭Ex dV, \iiint_E x\, dV, ∭E​xdV, where EEE is bounded by the paraboloid x=4y2+4z2x = 4y^2 + 4z^2x=4y2+4z2 and the plane x=4x = 4x=4.

Notation used in this solution

SymbolMeaning
dVdVdV Volume element. In the order we use, dV=dy dz dxdV = dy\,dz\,dxdV=dydzdx is the small box of volume spanned by the differentials dydydy, dzdzdz, dxdxdx.
∭E\iiint_E∭E​ Triples integral over the solid region EEE. The three integrations run through the three spatial directions once each.
paraboloid A surface obtained by rotating a parabola about its axis of symmetry. Here x=4y2+4z2x = 4y^2 + 4z^2x=4y2+4z2 opens in the +x+x+x direction with vertex at the origin.
(y0,z0)(y_0,z_0)(y0​,z0​), rrr Polar coordinates in the yzyzyz-plane: y=rcos⁡θy = r\cos\thetay=rcosθ, z=rsin⁡θz = r\sin\thetaz=rsinθ, so y2+z2=r2y^2 + z^2 = r^2y2+z2=r2 and dy dz=r dr dθdy\,dz = r\,dr\,d\thetadydz=rdrdθ.
θ\thetaθ The angle from the positive yyy-axis in the yzyzyz-plane, 0≤θ≤2π0 \le \theta \le 2\pi0≤θ≤2π for a full turn.

Part 1 — Set up and evaluate

Step 1.1: Describe the solid.

The paraboloid x=4y2+4z2x = 4y^2 + 4z^2x=4y2+4z2 opens toward +x+x+x and the plane x=4x = 4x=4 caps it. The solid EEE is the set of points between them, i.e. 4y2+4z2≤x≤44y^2 + 4z^2 \le x \le 44y2+4z2≤x≤4, which is nonempty exactly for 0≤x≤40 \le x \le 40≤x≤4.

At a fixed height x=x0x = x_0x=x0​ the cross section is the disk y2+z2≤x0/4y^2 + z^2 \le x_0/4y2+z2≤x0​/4 in the plane x=x0x = x_0x=x0​, of radius r0=x0/2r_0 = \sqrt{x_0}/2r0​=x0​​/2.

Step 1.2: Choose the order of integration.

Because every cross section perpendicular to the xxx-axis is a full disk, we integrate in the yzyzyz-plane first (polar) and xxx last:

∭Ex dV=∫04∫02π∫0x/2x  r dr dθ dx. \iiint_E x\,dV = \int_0^4 \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^{\sqrt{x}/2} x\; r\, dr\, d\theta\, dx. ∭E​xdV=∫04​∫02π​∫0x​/2​xrdrdθdx.

Explanation of the limits: 0≤x≤40 \le x \le 40≤x≤4 spans the solid from the vertex to the cap; 0≤θ≤2π0 \le \theta \le 2\pi0≤θ≤2π runs once around the disk; 0≤r≤x/20 \le r \le \sqrt{x}/20≤r≤x​/2 because r2=y2+z2≤x/4r^2 = y^2+z^2 \le x/4r2=y2+z2≤x/4. The factor rrr is the Jacobian of the polar map in the yzyzyz-plane.

Step 1.3: Evaluate the inner integrals.

∫0x/2x r dr=x r22∣0x/2=x⋅x/42=x28, \int_0^{\sqrt{x}/2} x\,r\,dr = x\,\frac{r^2}{2}\bigg|_0^{\sqrt{x}/2} = x\cdot\frac{x/4}{2} = \frac{x^2}{8}, ∫0x​/2​xrdr=x2r2​​0x​/2​=x⋅2x/4​=8x2​, ∫02πx28 dθ=x28⋅2π=πx24. \int_0^{2\pi} \frac{x^2}{8}\,d\theta = \frac{x^2}{8}\cdot 2\pi = \frac{\pi x^2}{4}. ∫02π​8x2​dθ=8x2​⋅2π=4πx2​.

Step 1.4: Evaluate the outer integral.

∫04πx24 dx=π4⋅x33∣04=π4⋅643=16π3. \int_0^4 \frac{\pi x^2}{4}\,dx = \frac{\pi}{4}\cdot\frac{x^3}{3}\bigg|_0^4 = \frac{\pi}{4}\cdot\frac{64}{3} = \frac{16\pi}{3}. ∫04​4πx2​dx=4π​⋅3x3​​04​=4π​⋅364​=316π​.

Result. ∭Ex dV=16π3≈16.7552. \iiint_E x\, dV = \frac{16\pi}{3} \approx 16.7552. ∭E​xdV=316π​≈16.7552.

Step 1.5: Verification by Python.

The script solution/part1_step1.py evaluates the same integral twice with SymPy: directly, by slicing into disks of area πx/4\pi x/4πx/4, and independently as the full iterated polar integral. Both calls return the exact value 16π/316\pi/316π/3, confirming the hand derivation above. The figure scripts part1_figure1.py and part1_figure2.py produce the two figures embedded above.
